findings.issue: actions/checkout keeps its default persist-credentials: true, so the read-only GITHUB_TOKEN is written to .git/config while repository code runs (npm run playtest:million). There is no reachable path to misuse it: the token is contents: read, the job only runs on workflow_dispatch by someone with write access, and nothing is downloaded (no npm ci). This matches the existing million.yml.
findings.evidence: workflow_dispatch (trusted maintainer) -> checkout (token persisted, read-only) -> npm run playtest:million -- --lineups (repo code only)
findings.fix: Optional hygiene: add `with: persist-credentials: false` to the checkout step (and to million.yml too, for consistency).

summary: No BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR findings. Workflow: only workflow_dispatch triggers it (no schedule, push or pull_request_target), it has top-level permissions contents: read, both actions are pinned to full commit SHAs that match the other workflows, it uses no secrets, and there is no ${{ }} expression, so no expression injection is possible. It has a 30-minute timeout and does not run npm ci. CLI: --lineups is a fixed boolean flag and is rejected if given twice. --hands is checked against /^[0-9]+$/ and the bounds 27..1e9 with --lineups (9..1e9 without). --help combined with --lineups gives an error. Each shard's --lineup value comes from the fixed list LINEUP_SHARD_PRESETS (never from user input) and goes to spawn as an args array with no shell. The child cli.ts also checks --lineup against an own-property allow-list. Earlier showdowns: the runner fills them only from showdownOf(final). showdownOf returns null for fold-outs and copies only state.result.showdown, which the engine fills from revealShown. That function returns only seats that actually showed, so mucked hands and folded seats never reach it. The list is public information shared by every seat, holds at most 1000 entries per table (O(1) memory), and is reset when the table restarts. A new array is built on each append, so earlier views are not changed. Randomness is a deterministic seeded PRNG used for replayable simulation; nothing depends on it for security. No new dependencies.
